title: Graceful SSE fragment buffering and deterministic function-call ordering
author: Avery Chen
commits: Initial implementation: introduce fragment buffer and resume latch, add event seq tag
Parser update: avoid delimiter collision inside structured output and escape sequences
Adapter: wire up ordered toolcall queue and deterministic flush policy
Tests: end-to-end resume integration + fuzzed partial-json cases
Docs: streaming.md update and migration notes
review_comments: Priya Kumar: Can you explain how the resume latch behaves under repeated transient disconnects? Will fragments accumulate unbounded?

Avery Chen: The latch incurs a small per-connection buffer cap (configurable, default 128KB) and exposes backpressure via the existing ACK window. On repeated disconnects we persist the fragment ledger up to the cap and emit a resumable token to the client. If the cap is exceeded the oldest partial frames are checkpointed and a warning metric is emitted.

Marco Alvarez: The deterministic toolcall queue looks good. Two requests: add a small unit test to validate event ordering when fragments arrive out-of-order, and make sure the queue drains before connection close.
Avery Chen: Added test_sse_resume.py::test_toolcall_ordering and added explicit drain on graceful shutdown. Also wired metrics for queue length.
Lina Ortiz: Observability YAML should expose the new sse.resume.* metrics — approved after that change.
Avery Chen: Exposed sse.resume.buffered_bytes and sse.resume.resume_count in pkg/observability/metrics.yaml.
description:
Motivation: Streaming endpoints were occasionally producing truncated/partial JSON payloads and non-deterministic ordering for function/tool call events when TCP segmentation or proxy buffering split SSE frames. This caused downstream SDKs to mis-reconstruct structured outputs and tool invocations. This PR introduces a small, production-focused feature set to eliminate a class of these failures while keeping latency and cost impact minimal.

Design and changes: 1) Fragment buffer & resume latch: introduce a per-connection fragment buffer with a resumable latch. When a chunk ends mid-JSON (or mid-utf8), we hold the trailing bytes in the buffer and only expose complete JSON spans to the higher-level parser. On transient disconnects a resumable token is returned so clients can resume from the last acknowledged span. The buffer is bounded and configurable; when the buffer limit is reached we checkpoint the oldest partial spans and emit sse.resume.truncate_count metric.

2) Event-level sequence tags: each SSE logical event now carries a small seq tag (local to the connection) so reassembly is order-aware. This enables deterministic reordering in the reassembler without changing the external API. The tag is stripped before emitting to the existing OpenAI-compatible adapter.

3) Deterministic function-call handoff: tool/function call events are queued in an ordered handoff queue that relies on the seq tag. The queue guarantees in-order delivery to the tool runner even if fragments arrive interleaved or replayed by proxies. Graceful shutdown drains the queue; forced shutdown will emit sse.toolcall.dropped_count.

4) Structured output delimiter escaping: updated the parser to sanitize and escape OpenAI-compatible delimiters when they appear inside structured output blocks so that delimiting heuristics do not split valid JSON. This reduces false-positive partial-json detection.

Testing: Added unit and integration tests covering: (a) partial-json resume across disconnect/reconnect, (b) out-of-order fragment arrival with seq reordering, (c) toolcall ordering under fragmentation, (d) fuzzed partial JSON cases hitting earlier production incidents. CI ran full suite; fuzz harness exercised previously flaky cases deterministically.

Performance and compatibility: Microbenchmarks show <2% median latency change for 512-token streams and negligible throughput impact for typical workloads since buffering only retains small trailing fragments. Backwards compatibility preserved: clients that do not support resumable tokens continue to receive data as before; the seq tags are internal and stripped by the adapter.

Rollout plan: 1) Roll out feature behind runtime flag default-on for selected canary clusters, 2) Monitor sse.resume.* metrics and toolcall ordering SLIs for 72h, 3) If anomalies detected, flip runtime flag off which restores previous behavior immediately.

Checklist: - [x] Implementation in reassembler and adapter - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration tests + fuzz harness - [x] Metrics and docs updated - [x] Reviewed and approved by runtime and compat owners

Related: ENG-1982 (streaming resume), ENG-2057 (toolcall ordering).
release_notes: Fixes: stable reassembly of SSE fragments that previously produced partial/invalid JSON and nondeterministic function/toolcall ordering. Adds resumable fragments (client token), new sse.resume.* metrics, and internal seq tags for deterministic reordering.
notes: Migration: no client changes required; resumable token is opt-in by client when reconnecting
Follow-up: consider exposing resumable token TTL and server-side persistence options (ENG-2104)
